title: Typed rejections for revoked writes, impossible credit, stale epochs, stalled children and per-object caps

cases.summary: Adversarial attach/input on the real binary with a 64 KiB QA output ring: an observe-only viewer naming the writer's lease is forbidden; attach.credit acknowledging u64::MAX is invalid_credit, a numeric acknowledgement invalid_params and an unknown stream stream_not_found. A program that prints fake 'state: idle' and prompt text leaves the declared status never-reported; the next command's output is fenced (its bytes at matched_at read back) and terminal.screen's head equals that fence, so every later cursor is relative to bytes this run produced. A takeover with a stale epoch is lease_epoch_mismatch; the explicit takeover revokes the writer, whose queued write on the revoked lease is no_lease. A bracketed paste the program never enabled is paste_refused. An output wait armed before 300 000 bytes overflow the ring still matches the marker printed after them; the same cursor afterwards is cursor_expired, terminal.output from it resumes at the floor with gap true, a start past the head is invalid_params and a numeric offset invalid_params at params.from_offset. Under a child that never reads its PTY (stty -echo -icanon; sleep), two 64 KiB writes are admitted at sequences 1 and 2, the barrier on 2 is not reached with bytes pending, an Escape is ordered at sequence 3, the exit wait times out and the same pid is still running. Five 3 MiB writes are then admitted at sequences 4-8, the sixth is input_overflow before the advertised 16 MiB per-terminal input queue is exceeded, and the barrier on 8 reports the pending bytes still inside that budget. An argv element over 32 KiB is too_large naming argv_element_bytes before any spawn (t3 is not_found). Two writers (owner and writer principals, no lease) then alternate four submissions into a child that does not read (stty -icanon noflsh) at sequences 1-4; nothing is delivered until ctrl+c releases it, after which the program reads exactly one-a, two-a, one-b, two-b, each submission whole and in admission order. A program that stops right after a carriage return inside an open CSI sequence gives a late observer a first paint that reports checkpoint_inexact (inexact: [control_inside_open_sequence]); once the sequence completes, the repaint is exact again.

params.text: head -c 300000 /dev/zero | tr '\000' z; echo; echo flood-$((5*5))

argv: stty -echo -icanon noflsh; trap 'exec cat' INT; printf STALLED; while :; do sleep 1; done
